record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension 2m+1, and let M[i] be the finite covers coming from a finite-index normal chain of π_1(M). Must M be det-L2-acyclic, and must the alternating normalized logarithmic torsion sum over all degrees converge to the L2-torsion according to 2 ∑_{n=0}^{m+1} (-1)^n ln|tors H_n(M[i]; Z)|/[G:G_i] → ρ^{(2)}(M̃)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.11 (Modified Homological torsion growth and L2-torsion). Let M be an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension dim(M) = 2m + 1. Then M is det-L2-acyclic, the limit ... exists and is given by lim i→∞ 2 Σ_{n=0}^{m+1} (−1)^n · ln |tors Hn(M[i]; Z)| / [G : Gi] = ρ(2)(Mf).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be an aspherical closed manifold of odd dimension $\dim(M) = 2m+1$, with fundamental group $G = \pi_1(M)$ and universal cover $\widetilde{M}$. Suppose $(G_i)_{i\ge 0}$ is a descending chain of finite-index normal subgroups of $G$ with $\bigcap_i G_i = \{1\}$, and let $M[i] \to M$ denote the finite covering associated to $G_i$.

Recall:
- $\widetilde{M}$ is called det-$L^2$-acyclic if all its $L^2$-Betti numbers vanish and the Fuglede–Kadison determinant class condition holds, so that the $L^2$-torsion $\rho^{(2)}(\widetilde{M}) \in \mathbb{R}$ is defined.
- For a finitely generated abelian group $A$, $\mathrm{tors}\,A$ denotes its torsion subgroup, and $|\mathrm{tors}\,A|$ its order.

Prove or disprove the following two assertions:

(i) $\widetilde{M}$ is det-$L^2$-acyclic.

(ii) The limit exists and satisfies
$$\lim_{i \to \infty} \, 2 \sum_{n=0}^{m+1} (-1)^n \, \frac{\ln |\mathrm{tors}\, H_n(M[i]; \mathbb{Z})|}{[G : G_i]} \;=\; \rho^{(2)}(\widetilde{M}).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. It is a modified (weaker) version of Lück's homological torsion growth conjecture for aspherical manifolds. Surveys on $L^2$-torsion list it as a conjecture, and related works note that no finitely presented residually finite group is currently known to exhibit even exponential torsion growth in dimension one along a residual chain, indicating the general case is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on L2-torsion (Lück)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the homological torsion growth and L2-torsion conjecture and its modified versions for aspherical closed odd-dimensional manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as a conjecture without proof in recent survey on L2-torsion.

status_evidence.title: Mod p and torsion homology growth in nonpositive curvature
status_evidence.snippet: No finitely presented residually finite group is currently known to exhibit exponential homological torsion growth in dimension one along a residual chain of finite-index normal subgroups.
status_evidence.claim: General torsion growth behavior conjectured by Lück remains unverified in broad generality.
